question: What is Walmart's total debt (short and long term, including finance leases) and its net debt or net cash, and how are interest expense and interest coverage trending?

answer.summary: Walmart's total debt was $40.46B as of January 31, 2024, up 3.2% from $39.21B a year earlier [F01863][F01862]. Net debt was $30.59B at both FY2023 and FY2024, meaning the company carries net debt (not net cash) and it remained flat YoY [F01864][F01865]. Interest expense rose sharply to $2.26B in FY2024, up 26.4% YoY from $1.79B [F00021][F00022], following a 6.8% increase in FY2023 [F00022]. Interest coverage declined from 15.50x in FY2022 to 11.43x in FY2023 (-26.2%), then improved modestly to 11.96x in FY2024 (+4.6%) [F01870][F01871][F01872]. Debt-to-equity improved to 0.48x from 0.51x [F01866][F01867], while finance lease liabilities grew 17.9-27.9% YoY to $6.43B total [F00789][F00141][F00133].
drivers: Interest expense growth of 26.4% in FY2024, with short-term borrowings' weighted-average interest rate rising from 6.6% to 7.7% [T00510]
Net debt flat at $30.59B as total debt growth was offset by cash and investments [F01865]
Interest coverage improved +4.6% in FY2024 after a -26.2% decline in FY2023 [F01872][F01871]
Debt-to-equity improved -5.6% YoY to 0.48x as equity grew faster than debt [F01867]
risks_and_red_flags: Interest expense spiked 26.4% YoY in FY2024 to $2.26B, a 31% inflection vs the prior-2-period average [F00021]
Interest coverage down 23% over the FY2022-FY2024 window, from 15.50x to 11.96x [F01870][F01872]
Finance lease liabilities growing 17.9-27.9% YoY, with noncurrent rising from $4.84B to $5.71B [F00141][F00133]
Short-term borrowings doubled from $0.4B to $0.9B, with the weighted-average rate climbing from 6.6% to 7.7% [T00510]
data_quality_notes: Net debt is positive $30.59B, so it represents net debt rather than net cash [F01865]

outlook.actuals_view: Debt and net debt are stable while interest expense is rising sharply, compressing coverage; leverage ratio (debt-to-equity) improved modestly
